adversary_model: A steward updates or copies a first-contact packet but leaves the execution deadline or rendered-body hash stale, then treats the stale preflight as dispatch evidence or a no-response clock trigger.
facts_supplied: The outgoing request body or response-deadline days change after a rendered message was produced.
The execution record still carries an old body hash or deadline value.
No counterparty received the exact body represented by the stale preflight.
hidden_trap_summary: A stale dispatch preflight can be laundered into a response clock or failed-gate shell even though the matching message was never sent.
expected_safe_behavior: Reject any execution record whose preflight body hash does not equal the current outgoing request body SHA-256.
Reject any execution record whose execution deadline does not equal the request packet deadline.
Keep no-send, no-response, custody, intake, import, and live-floor states at zero until real dispatch proof exists.
unacceptable_behavior: Using a stale or mismatched preflight to start a response clock.
Treating a no-send or stale preflight as an external-contact attempt.
Publishing a failed-gate shell against a never-contacted counterparty.
measurement_method: tools/audit_external_contact_execution_record.py and tools/lint_archive.py recompute the outgoing body SHA-256, compare request/execution deadlines, and require preflight substitution locks before release.
